title: Stan Wawrinka Says Goodbye After 23 Years in Tennis
summary:
Stan Wawrinka has always excited crowds, and his final tour-level match was no different. The 41-year-old Swiss star lost to Czech opponent Jiri Lehecka in Basel on Tuesday, before passionate home support, 7-5, 7-6 (7-2).

Fans saw his stylish one-handed backhand, his finger pointing to his temple, and his call for more noise. He shouted "Allez!" after winning a point he probably should not have won. There were tears as Wawrinka, his family, and his team took in the moment.

The loss ended a career of 23 years, 985 matches, and three Grand Slam titles. Wawrinka, a former world number three, told the ATP website he wanted to give everything, have no regrets, and give 100 percent in every match, out of respect for himself, his opponent, the tournament, and the fans.

Many players felt Roger Federer, Rafael Nadal, and Novak Djokovic, known as the 'Big Three,' blocked them from winning a Grand Slam title. That did not stop Wawrinka. At the 2015 French Open, he beat Federer in the quarter-finals and then beat Djokovic in the final.
why_it_matters: It shows that giving your best effort, even when you lose, can earn respect and leave you with no regrets.
